facts.statement: Zapalasaurus is an extinct sauropod dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous La Amarga Formation in modern-day Patagonia.
facts.quote: Zapalasaurus is an extinct genus of sauropod dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous-aged La Amarga Formation of what is today Patagonia.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen includes a middle neck vertebra, a sacral fragment, 17 tail vertebrae, parts of the pelvis, and partial leg bones.
facts.quote: The holotype of Zapalasaurus consists of a single vertebrae from the middle of the neck, a fragment of a sacral vertebra, 17 caudal vertebrae, the left ischium and pubis, a fragment of an ilium, a partial left femur, and the left tibia.

facts.statement: Zapalasaurus is distinguished by features in its neck vertebrae and tail vertebrae that double in length from front to back.
facts.quote: Zapalasaurus can be distinguished from other diplodocoids based on several features of the cervical neural arches as well as caudal vertebrae which double in length from front to back.

facts.statement: Researchers assume Zapalasaurus had a long neck adapted to swing in an arc shape for feeding.
facts.quote: Zapalasaurus is assumed to have a long neck which would have been developed for feeding adaption, allowing its neck to swing in an arc like shape.

facts.statement: Fossils of Zapalasaurus were discovered in 1995 at a site called Puesto Morales.
facts.quote: The fossils which would eventually be named Zapalasaurus were discovered in 1995 at a locality called Puesto Morales.

facts.statement: The specimen was excavated between 1995 and 1996 under the leadership of paleontologist José F. Bonaparte.
facts.quote: The specimen was excavated from 1995-1996 by scientists associated with the Bernardino Rivadavia Natural Sciences Argentine Museum and the Juan A. Olsacher Museum under the leadership of the famous Argentine paleontologist José F. Bonaparte.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen is designated Pv-6127-MOZ.
facts.quote: The specimen was given the designation Pv-6127-MOZ.

facts.statement: Zapalasaurus was formally described and named in 2006 by a team led by Leonardo Salgado.
facts.quote: It was described and named in 2006 by a team of scientists led by Leonardo Salgado.

facts.statement: The genus name Zapalasaurus honors the city of Zapala, located about 80 km from the discovery site.
facts.quote: Zapalasaurus was named after the city of Zapala, which is approximately 80 km away from where the holotype was discovered.

facts.statement: The species name bonapartei honors the Argentine paleontologist Dr. José Bonaparte.
facts.quote: The species epithet was given in honor of Dr. José Bonaparte, who was an important Argentine paleontologist in the 20th century.

facts.statement: The holotype comes from alluvial plain deposits in the upper Piedra Parada Member, representing the first fossil record for that unit.
facts.quote: El holotipo, Pv-6127-MOZ, provendría de depósitos fangosos de llanura aluvial ubicados en los tramos superiores del Miembro Piedra Parada de dicha formación, constituyendo el primer registro fósil para la citada unidad.

facts.statement: The fossil consists of a skeleton without a skull.
facts.quote: El fósil consiste en un esqueleto sin cráneo.

facts.statement: Additional material was found in 2004.
facts.quote: En 2004 se encontró material adicional.

facts.statement: Zapalasaurus lived during the Barremian and late Aptian stages of the Early Cretaceous in the Neuquén Basin.
facts.quote: Zapalasaurus was discovered in sedimentary rocks of the La Amarga Formation, which is part of the Neuquén Basin and dates to the Barremian and late Aptian of the Early Cretaceous.

facts.statement: Zapalasaurus lived between 130 and 122 million years ago in what is now South America.
facts.quote: que vivió a principios y mediados del período Cretácico, entre 130 y 122 millones de años, desde el Barremiense al Aptiense, en lo que es hoy Sudamérica.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest Zapalasaurus likely fed at ground level.
facts.quote: Rebbachisaurids like Zapalasaurus presumably fed at ground-level, while basal Titanosauriforms exploited food sources at higher levels.

facts.statement: While originally thought to be a basal diplodocoid, later analyses classify Zapalasaurus as a member of Rebbachisauridae.
facts.quote: In their original description, Salgado and colleagues found Zapalasaurus to be a basally-branching diplodocoid outside of any of the major subgroups. However, subsequent analyses have found it to be a member of Rebbachisauridae.

facts.statement: Zapalasaurus was initially considered the sister group to other Diplodocoidea but is now firmly placed within Rebbachisauridae.
facts.quote: Zapalasaurus bonapartei fue considerado inicialmente como el grupo hermano de los demás Diplodocoidea, excluyendo a Haplocanthosaurus, pero últimamente se ha consolidado como rebaquisáurido.

facts.statement: Zapalasaurus shares features with Rebbachisaurids, including anterior tail vertebrae with well-developed dorsal transverse process components.
facts.quote: Con ellos comparte unas vértebras caudales anteriores con componente dorsal del proceso transverso bien desarrollado.

facts.statement: A femoral head diameter of 30.5 cm indicates an estimated body length of about 15 meters.
facts.quote: La cabeza del fémur tenía un diámetro de 30,5 centímetros, lo que indica una longitud corporal de unos 15 metros.

facts.statement: Zapalasaurus possesses unique autapomorphies, including specific neural arch structures and tail vertebrae that double in length over the first 20.
facts.quote: Exhibe una serie de caracteres que son interpretados como autapomórficos: arcos neurales cervicales con una lámina uniendo la prezigapófisis y el sector zigapofisial de la lámina postzigodiapofisial; arco neurales cervicales con la lámina postzigodiapofisial reducida en su sector diapofisial; aros neurales cervicales con la lámina espinoprezigapofisial pobremente desarrollada, que no alcanza el extremo de la espina neural; vértebras caudales medias y posteriores con la espina neural anteroposteriormente alargada, cuyo extremo anterior se ubica a un nivel más alto que el extremo posterior; vértebras caudales duplican su largo en las 20 primeras vértebras.

facts.statement: The discovery of Zapalasaurus suggests that basal diplodocoid diversity in Early Cretaceous South America was greater than previously thought.
facts.quote: Hasta la fecha, el registro de saurópodos en la parte alta del Cretácico Inferior de Patagonia consistía en un único grupo de diplodocoides, los rebaquisáuridos, representados por dos géneros estrechamente relacionados, Limaysaurus y Rayososaurus. El registro de Agustinia, un posible diplodocoide y Zapalasaurus hace suponer que la diversidad de diplodocoides basales en la parten alta del Cretácico Inferior de Sudamérica es mayor de lo que se pensaba.

facts.statement: Evidence suggests that in Early Cretaceous South America, diplodocoids were at least as abundant and diverse as titanosauriforms.
facts.quote: Según parece, en el Cretácico Inferior de Sudamérica los diplodocoides fueron al menos tan abundantes y diversos como los titanosauriformes.
